chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Royalties and tune credits
summary: He has collected royalties since 1929 on his own tunes and explains how leaders took credit in the past.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: No, I ... I've been collecting royalties since 1929. I wrote how many tunes?
How many tunes have you written?
I don't really -- got to check them out. But, I've been collecting twice a year since 1929.
From where? From where? From Where?
From Higginbotham Blues, Give Me Your Telephone Number and a guy will call me up and say ... and there's some other tunes. I don't know. played the record the other day swing out,
You don't know how many tunes you've written.
I sure don't. I know how many I wrote, four?
Four tunes?
Where is the money coming from?
Oh, it comes from the royalty companies. They have to send me the money.
What publishing company?
I don't know. ( ? ) I think ... Higginbotham Blues is on an OKeh record. I'm sure of that because it was 9 o'clock in the morning
But you don't know like (..?)
What they did after that, you see the government took over.
Oket records?

On all the records. You write a tune, you're going to get paid for it today. Once upon a time, you know, its like, I'm with a band and I think up a tune and I tell the leader, And the leader says to me, "Well, if you let me put my name on that, so and so and so and so, I will record it for you." And that's the way you did it. They'll get it to you.
Did Luis Russell, did he do things like that?
No.
Louis Armstrong?
No, he wasn't like that.
What about Louis Armstrong?
No.
What about Fletcher Henderson?
I don't remember. No.
But that was a common practice at that time like you and write a tune, what about even playing it on a bandstand?
Well, they don't ask for nothing.
Well, the band leaders would let you play that tune on the bandstand, I mean if he liked it or something?
well, he's gonna play it, ... I mean if the leader said, "Play it," the leader made the arrangement. He said, "We're going to play this."
So you didn't make the arrangements on your tunes or anything?
No, I didn't make arrangements.
On your tunes, on your Blues and so forth, who gets the credit for that?
I do, cause I'm on it.
Does anybody else ...

... over and over and over again until the guy listens and you put it down and that's the way we get 'em like that. I have a tune now I wrote when I was in the hospital. It's a good one, too. You better do your thinking before you start your drinking, ... I got the lyrics to it; nobody knows about it but me.
You got to give it to Donald or myself and maybe we can record it ourselves or get someone to record it for you.
Maybe. We'll see about it.
